Dans cette section, nous nous intéressons aux éléments phoniques (autres que les phonèmes) qui ont une fonction distinctive : le ton, l’accent, l’intonation et le rythme La langue mbochi ne possède pas de structuration accentuelle ou rythmique qui puisse déterminer des groupements de la taille du Groupe. (Aborobongui 2011 :11, Rialland et al. 2009, Embanga et al. 2011). Aussi allons-nous parler des tons et des syllabes. [...] 1.1.2.2. Tonologie. Dans cette section, nous parlons des tonèmes du parler mbochi olee. Comme bien d’autres langues de son groupe, le mbochi est une langue à tons. C'est-à-dire, on peut y opposer des mots par ailleurs identiques mais se distinguant par la variation de la hauteur mélodique.

new_statements.translation: 1.1.2. Prosody. In this section we consider the phonic elements (other than phonemes) that have a distinctive function: tone, accent/stress, intonation and rhythm. The Mbochi language has no accentual or rhythmic structuring that could determine groupings of the size of the [phonological] Group (Aborobongui 2011:11, Rialland et al. 2009, Embanga et al. 2011). We shall therefore speak of tones and syllables. [...] [p.70] Like many other languages of its group, Mbochi is a tone language; that is, words otherwise identical can be opposed solely by a difference in pitch.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Mbochi is described as a two-tone language (H vs L, TBU = mora/syllable, lexical and grammatical tone) with no accentual (stress) or rhythmic organisation; the author explicitly sets accent and rhythm aside as non-existent in the language and treats only tone and syllable structure as distinctive prosodic units. No stress position is posited anywhere in the 555-page description of the ten dialects.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The statement is made for 'la langue mbochi' generally within the chapter on the Olee (Boundji) reference dialect; the dialect-comparison chapters discuss only segmental and tonal variation.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns word/phrase prosody generally: absence of accentual structure is invoked to explain why prosodic grouping (Groupe Phonologique / Groupe Intonatif, after Rialland & Aborobongui) is defined by hiatus resolution, tone processes and boundary tones rather than by stress. It is a brief assertion resting on cited conference work by Rialland & Embanga Aborobongui rather than on the author's own argumentation, though the author is a native-speaker linguist describing his own field data.
new_statements.identity_note: Kouarata's phonology chapter (Part II ch.1 sec.1.1) is headed 'Analyse phonologique du parler Olee' (the Boundji/Olee variety, his reference dialect, C25B in his internal numbering), but the deciding sentence is phrased for 'la langue mbochi' as a whole and the thesis covers all ten dialects (Olee, Mbondzi, Tsambitso, Ngilima, Bokwele, Bonyala, Ngae, Obaa, Eboyi, Ondinga). Aborobongui 2013 describes the Mbondzi variety; Bedrosian 1996/97 and Fontaney 1988 describe Boundji/Olee. All fall under mbos1242 (ISO mdw).
